data.title: Airbnb Stock (ABNB) Rises 18% and Hits Highest Level in Four Years
data.description:
The stock of Airbnb (ABNB) rose 18% on Aug. 7 and closed at $178 a share, its highest level in four years, after the company reported blockbuster financial results.

Airbnb stock was one of the best performers in the market on the day after the homestay and short-term rental company delivered a beat-and-raise quarter and said that its booking platform is getting a lift from the integration of artificial intelligence (AI).

Management at Airbnb credited an accelerated pace of bookings and continued strong travel demand for the strong second-quarter results. "Despite the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, we continue to ​see strong underlying demand globally," said finance chief Elinor Mertz on the company's earnings call with analysts and investors.

Airbnb's Blowout Quarter

Airbnb reported earnings per share (EPS) of $1.37, which beat the consensus estimate among analysts of $1.22. Revenue in the spring quarter totaled $3.6 billion, which topped estimates of $3.58 billion. Sales were up 17% from a year ago.

The vacation rental company also raised its full-year guidance for revenue growth and its profit margin, saying it now expects revenue growth to increase "at least mid-teens," supported by the accelerated pace of nights and seats booked. It also now expects a full-year profit margin of at least 35.5%.

"AI is ​the best ⁠thing to ever happen to Airbnb," said CEO Brian Chesky on the company's earnings call.

Is ABNB Stock a Buy?

Airbnb's stock has a consensus Moderate Buy rating among 33 Wall Street analysts. That rating is based on 20 Buy, 12 Hold, and one Sell recommendations issued in the last three months. The average ABNB price target of $174.50 implies 2% downside from current levels.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Does the U.K. Deal Mean Trouble? Paramount Skydance (NASDAQ:PSKY) Stock Gains Regardless
data.description:
When news emerged that the United Kingdom's various regulators had signed off on entertainment giant Paramount Skydance's (PSKY) merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), some thought it was a good sign. But others think it may be the beginning of the end for the deal after all. Investors seemed optimistic, though, and gave Paramount shares an extra 2% in the closing minutes of Friday's trading.

When the Competition and Markets Authority let the deal go through, some figured that this was one more nail in the coffin of the states' case. After all, when this many markets are letting the deal go through, even with some concessions and assurances, suggesting that the deal is somehow a competition-killer looks like a long shot. But some believe that it is those very same concessions that give the states' argument against the deal weight.

Basically, the idea that Paramount's deal requires concessions to go through in the U.K., where its market share is significantly lower than it is in the United States, suggests that the deal is much more dangerous in a market where Paramount's market share is much higher and the market more concentrated. But given that the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) already allowed the deal through, that argument loses some weight.

Paramount+ Outage

And right at the same time that Paramount is trying to get its deal through, its flagship streaming operation, Paramount+, suffered an outage. Starting from around nine this morning, and continuing until about noon, users reported errors with video streaming. Some also found problems with the app itself, suggesting that the problem was more widespread than some might have expected.

But based on further information, the problem seemed mostly resolved by early afternoon, with only a comparative handful of issues reported after the largest number of reports. Any outage is a bad one when it comes to streaming services, but it also represents an opportunity for above-and-beyond customer service. If Paramount is quick to offer outage credits here, then it might keep some users in the fold, even as users regularly switch from one provider to another.

Is Paramount Stock a Good Buy Right Now?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Hold consensus rating on PSKY stock based on two Buys, four Holds and three Sells assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. After a 13.8% loss in its share price over the past year, the average PSKY price target of $10.50 per share implies 14.13% upside potential.
data.author: Steve Anderson

data.title: Burger King (QSR) Overtakes Wendy's to Become Second-Largest U.S. Burger Chain
data.description:
Burger King, owned by Restaurant Brands International (QSR), has surpassed Wendy's (WEN) to become the second-largest burger chain in America.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Burger King is now second only to McDonald's (MCD) when it comes to systemwide sales among burger restaurant chains in the U.S. Burger King had fallen out of second place and been overtaken by Wendy's six years ago amid declining sales at its U.S. restaurants.

However, Restaurant Brands International has invested heavily in a multi-year turnaround strategy at Burger King, and managed to revive the chain's fortunes, as evidenced by the company's recently reported second-quarter financial results.

The Revival of Burger King

Restaurant Brands reported strong second-quarter financial results due largely to a recovery in the Burger King chain. The Toronto-based company, which also owns Tim Hortons and Popeyes, said Burger King's U.S. same-store sales rose 8.5% year-over-year in Q2. International Burger King restaurants saw same-store sales growth of 5.4% during the quarter.

The growth comes after the burger chain underwent restaurant renovations and launched a new marketing campaign. "Burger King's performance is a great example of what's possible when you invest in the fundamentals and execute well," said Restaurant Brands CEO Josh Kobza in the company's earnings statement.

News that Burger King has moved into second place among U.S. burger chains also comes on the same day that Wendy's reported sluggish sales and announced that it is cutting its dividend in half. Management at Wendy's cited declining customer traffic and shrinking franchisee profits reasons for its poor results and the dividend cut. Wendy's sales were up only 1% from a year ago in the second quarter.

Is QSR Stock a Buy?

Restaurant Brands International's stock has a consensus Moderate Buy rating among 14 Wall Street analysts. That rating is based on 10 Buy and four Hold recommendations issued in the last three months. The average QSR price target of $85.64 implies 16% upside from current levels.

data.title: Why are Gold and Silver Up Today, 8/7/26?
data.description:
Both gold (XAUUSD) and silver (XAGUSD) are rallying on Friday as the uptrend for the precious metals continues.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Falling rate hike odds are supporting both gold and silver. When interest rates rise, holding precious metals becomes less attractive compared with interest-bearing assets like Treasuries. That's because precious metals don't generate interest, while bonds do. On the CME FedWatch tool, the odds of a 25-bps hike at the September 16 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting fell to 44.1% from 55% a day ago.

Jobs Report Weighs on Rate Hike Odds

Rate hike expectations took a tumble after the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) published July's jobs report. The data came in far weaker than expected, with nonfarm payrolls falling by 23,000 instead of the projected 80,000 gain. In addition, the labor force participation rate dropped to 61.4%, the lowest since February 2021. That contributed to the unemployment rate falling to 4.1% from 4.2% in June.

With a weaker labor market, the Fed is more inclined to hold rates steady or lower them. Lower rates support employment by reducing borrowing costs and encouraging businesses to invest and hire. However, expectations could shift once again after the BLS releases July's Consumer Price Index next Wednesday, as hotter-than-expected inflation could tilt rate hike odds higher.

data.title: Dow Jones Today: DJIA Edges Higher after Jobs Report Eases Rate Hike Odds
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is trading higher on Friday after the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) published July's jobs report.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

During the month, nonfarm payrolls decreased by 23,000, well below the consensus expectation of 80,000 additions. Furthermore, May and June's payrolls were revised lower by a combined 103,000 jobs.

The BLS also said the unemployment rate dropped to 4.1%, below the estimate of 4.2% and down from 4.2% in June. That appears good on the surface, although what actually happened is that the labor force participation rate fell to 61.4%, its lowest level since February 2021. In other words, the labor force shrank as fewer people sought work.

"This is a bleak jobs report," said Navy Federal Credit Union Chief Economist Heather Long. "The U.S. labor market is stalling again and that is going to make the Federal Reserve's job harder and life for job seekers rough."

Following the report, the odds of a 25-bps rate hike at the September 16 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting fell to 41.9% from 55%, according to the CME FedWatch tool. That provided a supporting hand to stocks, as higher rates reduce the present value of future earnings.

The report also makes the Fed's job more difficult. The central bank must now grapple with raising rates to tame inflation or lowering rates to stimulate the labor market. Of course, leaving rates unchanged is also on the table and is the most likely outcome at the September FOMC. Investors will receive a key inflation update next week when the BLS releases July's Consumer Price Index (CPI).

The Dow Jones is up by 0.16% at the time of writing.
data.author: Eddie Pan

data.title: Jersey Mike's Stock (JMKE) Continues to Struggle a Week After IPO
data.description:
The stock of restaurant chain Jersey Mike's (JMKE) continues to struggle and remains below its initial public offering (IPO) price of $23 per share.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

Two ETFs for long or short leverage on SPCX

The popular sub sandwich restaurant chain made its market debut on July 30 under the ticker symbol "JMKE." The shares had been price at $23 but began trading at $21 per share, which was 9% below the IPO pricing. A little more than a week later, and the shares are changing hands at $22.86 on Aug. 7.

Jersey Mike's sold 43.5 million shares as part of the IPO, raising $1 billion and valuing the company at $7.3 billion. The company is among the largest-ever IPOs for a U.S. restaurant chain and was one of the biggest non-tech market debuts of the year following the record-setting launch of SpaceX (SPCX). However, the stock has struggled to gain any traction following its IPO.

Reasons JMKE Stock Is Down

The reasons JMKE stock has failed to move higher since its market debut are varied and complicated. On one hand, the company has yet to report any financial results as a public company. Although the company did report in its IPO prospectus net income of $55 million and revenue of $724 million for 2025. The company also said that its same-store sales increased 3% year-over-year.

Another complicating factor is the current Cyclospora and Salmonella outbreaks at competing restaurant chains such as Yum! Brands-owned (YUM) Taco Bell and Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG). While no foodborne illnesses have been reported at Jersey Mike's, stocks of restaurant chains have declined over the past week in sympathy with Yum! Brands and Chipotle.

Jersey Mike's has not yet announced when it will report its first financial results as a public concern.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Hold Off on Buying Cloudflare After 'Stellar' $696 Million Update
data.description:
On Thursday evening, Cloudflare went to the tape with the firm's second-quarter financial results. For the period ended June 30, the cloud services and internet infrastructure provider posted an adjusted EPS of $0.29 (GAAP EPS: -$0.48) on revenue of $696.061 million. These top- and adjusted bottom-line results both beat Wall Street's expectations, while that sales number was good enough for year-over-year growth of 35.9%. The stock is running higher on these results. Let's take a look.

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

CEO and co-founder Matthew Prince commented on the quarter. Prince wrote:

"We delivered a stellar second quarter, highlighted by revenue accelerating to $696.1 million, up 36% year-over-year, and record growth in total paying customers, large customers and developers on our platform. As the web shifts to AI answer engines and agent-driven commerce, we are seeing a fundamental rewrite of the Internet for machine-to-machine traffic. Cloudflare sits at the center of this paradigm shift — building the infrastructure, controls, developer tools, and payment rails for the Agentic Internet."

Prince added:

"The business model of the web is changing, and no company is better positioned than Cloudflare to help define its future."

Operations

For the period, with sales up 35.9%, gross profit increased 30.2% to $499.517 million as gross margin dropped from 74.9% to 71.7%. Total GAAP operating expenses grew 56.4% to $705.213 million. This left a GAAP operating income/loss of -$205.696 million, down from -$67.264 million. After adjusting for stock-based compensation and the amortization of acquired intangibles, among other items, operating income lands at $96.111 million, up from $72.315 million. GAAP operating margin dropped from -13.1% to -29.6%. Adjusted operating margin dropped from 14.1% to 13.8%.

After accounting for interest, other income and expenses as well as for taxes, GAAP net income/loss printed at -$169.981 million, down from -$50.446 million. That works out to -$0.48 per fully diluted share, down from the year-ago comp of -$0.15. After adjustments, net income increased 43.6% to $107.78 million. That adjusted EPS hit the tape at $0.29, up from $0.21.

Guidance

For the current quarter, Cloudflare is projecting an adjusted EPS of $0.34, with revenue landing in between $736 million and $737 million. Wall Street was looking for $0.32 on $722.7 million, so this was a beat.

For the full year, the firm now expects to earn between $1.25 and $1.26 per share on an adjusted basis, up from previously issued guidance for $1.19 to $1.20. Full-year revenue is seen at $2.86 billion to $2.87 billion, also up from previously issued guidance. Consensus had been for an adjusted $1.20 per share on $2.81 billion in revenue. Another beat.

Fundamentals

For the period reported, Cloudflare generated operating cash flow of $117.564 million. Out of that number came traditional capex spending of $49.961 million and capitalized internal use software of $11.219 million. That left free cash flow of $56.384 million (+69.4%). Cloudflare does not return capital to shareholders.

Looking over the balance sheet, the firm ended the period with a cash position of $4.163 billion. This puts current assets at $4.778 billion. Current liabilities ended the quarter at $2.628 billion, including short-term debt of $1.293 billion, but also deferred revenues of $812.187 million. The firm's headline current ratio stands at a healthy 1.82. Adjusted for deferred revenues, that ratio rises to 2.63.

Total assets amount to $6.474 billion, of which only a small portion is labeled as either goodwill or other intangibles. Total liabilities less equity comes to $4.854 billion, including $684 million in longer-term debt. The firm can cover its entire debt load with its cash position. This balance sheet is strong.

Opinion

The quarter was solid, at least on an adjusted basis. Margins are under a bit of pressure. That said, the guidance is strong, cash flows are healthy, and the balance sheet is in very good shape. Wall Street is already on top of this one. ​
data.author: TheStreet Pro
